extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, and news organizations (potential nominators and nominees for the Taylor Fairness Award)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection principles for nominating and choosing journalism (daily newspaper) work judged exemplary for fairness; covers eligibility, what may be nominated, how entries will be evaluated, and procedural rules for nominators and selectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness as a core value tied to credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "When what a newspaper publishes is perceived by the public to be fair, then its coverage will be regarded as credible. These two values walk hand in hand."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is intended to spotlight journalism that demonstrates a commitment to fairness; nominations should reflect work that treats individuals and institutions fairly and pursues truth in a spirit of fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: No single definition of fairness (nominators apply their own standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is no definition of fairness in the guidelines for Taylor Fairness Award nominations. This is deliberate... The standards for fairness in journalism are complex and diverse and not easily defined for this kind of journalism competition."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominators are expected to apply their own standards of fairness and to provide a rationale on the nominating form; the program will collect these rationales to build knowledge about how fairness is perceived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Works must meet the highest standards of fairness (nominator judgment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominators will recommend efforts that in their judgment meet the highest standards of fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The nominator's judgment and written rationale are central to whether a work is put forward; the jurors will then consider the nominations when selecting the winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspects of journalistic process to be considered in selection
rubrics_metrics.description: "The award jury will then consider all aspects of the journalistic process in selecting the winner: reporting, writing, editing, headlines, photographs, illustrations and presentation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation is holistic: not just reporting but also editing, headline writing, visuals and how the material is presented; recognition acknowledges contributions across the news staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible forms of work (what may be nominated)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Nominators may recommend a single story or editorial or commentary, a series of stories or editorials or commentaries, or a body of work by an individual journalist."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are flexible in form — single pieces, series, or bodies of work — and should be nominated according to how they exemplify fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipients (who may receive the award)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The award can go to an individual journalist or to a newspaper or wire service."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes either individual achievement or institutional/collective efforts when multiple staff were involved in fair journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of contributors required for nominated work
rubrics_metrics.description: "Once work is nominated, a newspaper will be asked to identify each of the journalists who made significant contributions to the story or stories."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When nominated work involves multiple staff, the submitting organization must list significant contributors so proper credit can be considered by the jury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating panel composition and role
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations will come from a panel of 31 journalists, "a diverse group and includes many who have written about fairness and credibility or have participated in news industry examinations of these topics."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominators are established journalists (including those experienced with issues of fairness and credibility); they recommend works they believe meet high fairness standards and supply rationale on the nominating form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest exclusion for selectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Taylor family and no present or former journalist at The Boston Globe should participate in the process of selecting a winner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To preserve impartiality, family members and Globe-affiliated journalists are excluded from selection; the jury is separate from the Taylor family and Globe staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility timeframe and publication type
rubrics_metrics.description: "The first Taylor Fairness Award will be given in 2002, based on work published in daily newspapers during 2001."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominated work must have been published in daily newspapers during the specified eligibility year (for the inaugural award, 2001); submissions must meet the stated publication-type and timeframe requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative details: deadline and prize
rubrics_metrics.description: Bill Taylor has raised funds to endow an annual prize of $10,000. "Deadline for submissions is February 2, 2002."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominators must meet submission deadlines and other administrative requirements; prize amount and endowment details provided for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and public sharing to foster understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: The award aims to focus public attention on exemplary journalism that meets high standards of fairness and to build a collection of nominations to understand how fairness is perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected and leading nominated entries will be posted on the Nieman website and the program will invite reaction and comment from journalists and the public to use as a resource on fairness in journalism.
